historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue CAGR (5.3-5.4%) cross-checked against management's medium-term 'average mid-single-digit organic growth' guidance; equity CAGR rejected as a base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (19-22%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (5%) because the FY2021 base was crushed by GBP1.8bn of write-offs and restatements (FY21 equity GBP229m); it measures balance-sheet repair, not growth. EPS CAGRs are null: FY21 and FY23 statutory EPS were negative. Owner-FCF 3y CAGR (21.9%) is flattered by the non-cash Type 31 charge in the FY26 end point; the 5y owner-FCF CAGR is negative because FY21 reported FCF carried disposal-era working-capital inflows. None of the historical series is a usable forward base on its own.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - finance income): FY21 231.1, FY22 -211.5, FY23 104.9, FY24 137.8, FY25 137.1, FY26 189.9. SBC has grown 3.2 -> 17.2 (FY21-FY26) and finance income 16.6 -> 35.0, so owner FCF has grown slower than reported FCF (3y 21.9% vs 21.1% is a coincidence of a depressed base; the 5y gap -3.9% vs -0.7% shows the drift).

scenario_narratives.base: Babcock stays the sole-source through-life partner for the UK submarine fleet and the Devonport/Rosyth dockyards, grows revenue 6% in FY27 fading to 2.5% as the GBP9.8bn backlog is replenished at the medium-term 'mid-single-digit' pace, and lifts EBIT from 8.2% (FY26 ex-Type 31) to c.8.7% - short of the >9% target because the model keeps a 0.3-0.5pp allowance for the fixed-price charges that have recurred through the company's history (SDP, Ascent, Type 31). Cash tax normalises to 25% by FY31 as the deferred tax asset is used, Rosyth and advanced-manufacturing capex runs c.2.5% of revenue, and working capital consumes 15% of each year's revenue increase as contract advances unwind. The Type 31 cost-to-complete (c.GBP140m, FY27-FY29) and c.GBP20m p.a. of pension deficit repair are charged once, in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes are UK/NATO budget delivery and export conversion: defence spending reaches 2.5% of GDP on schedule with the 3% ambition legislated, SSN-AUKUS and the Virginia-class module work at Rosyth ramp on time, Indonesia's GBP4bn Maritime Partnership Programme and Poland buy Arrowhead 140 licences and ships, and Cavendish Nuclear's SMR/owner's-engineer roles compound at Nuclear's 9.5% margin. Growth holds at 7-8% for four years, EBIT reaches c.9.8% with no further material fixed-price charges, export deposits cut the working-capital drag, and the terminal multiple is capped at 17x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes are the UK MOD's fiscal position and Babcock's own fixed-price execution record: the Defence Investment Plan slips, the FMSP follow-on is re-priced on worse terms after the six-month bridging agreement, legacy Rail and South Africa keep shrinking, the Arrowhead export pipeline stays at letters of intent, and later-stage Type 31 outfitting, Virginia-class components or SMR engineering throw further GBP50-70m charges every couple of years. Growth settles at 2-3% nominal, EBIT stalls at c.7.3%, working capital stays a drag at -25% of growth, and the market pays 13x terminal FCF for a single-customer contractor that never hit its 9% margin.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Babcock as a sovereign-infrastructure services annuity with a recurring execution tax. The owner-FCF build is unlevered, ex-Type 31 and component-built (IFRS-16 EBITDA -> lease cash -> SBC -> D&A ex-ROU -> cash tax ramp -> capex -> negative working capital), discounted at a GBP WACC of 8.5% in every scenario; the risks the market worries about - fixed-price charges, MOD concentration, governance history - are priced in the flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a stacked WACC premium. One-off balance-sheet claims (Type 31 cost-to-complete, pension deficit repair, April buyback cash) are settled once in the bridge so the margin path stays a clean recurring-economics judgment.
key_risks_to_valuation: Further fixed-price programme charges (Type 31 later-ship outfitting, Virginia-class modules, SMR engineering) beyond the 0.3-0.5pp recurring allowance in the base margin path
FMSP follow-on contract re-priced or delayed - it is the largest single contract and sat on a six-month bridging agreement at 31 March 2026
UK Defence Investment Plan slippage under fiscal constraint; UK MOD is c.61% of revenue
Working-capital unwind of contract advances running larger than -15% of revenue growth (FY26 ex-charge was c.-GBP110m)
Cash tax normalising faster than the 12% -> 25% ramp if the deferred tax asset is consumed sooner
Terminal value is 50-60% of EV and the 15x cap binds in the base case; a lower exit multiple for a government contractor is the main single-parameter downside

inputs.share_count_basis: 505,596,597 shares in issue less 10,740,335 treasury at 31 Mar 2026 (FY26 AR p.~175) = 494.9m; less 4,410,766 bought into treasury when the GBP200m programme completed on 28 Apr 2026 (16,954,061 total less 12,543,295 in FY26) = 490.4m; plus 9.9m dilutive share-plan awards (diluted 511.1m less basic 501.3m weighted average, FY26 AR note 9) = 500.3m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. The second GBP200m buyback announced with FY26 results is not modelled (value-neutral at fair value).
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity share-based payments' GBP17.2m (FY25 GBP14.3m), note 24. No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed (UK plans settle from treasury/ESOT shares), so the combined figure equals the add-back.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence. No FX risk, no dual listing to parity-check; the only check is magnitude: a per-share value in the 5-15 GBP range must print as 500-1500p.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:35:38Z regular close (LSE); Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime unchanged on re-fetch 2026-10-05, no after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10y gilt c.4.5%, UK ERP 5.0%, beta c.1.0 for a UK defence/nuclear services contractor -> cost of equity c.9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt c.5.5% (GBP300m 2026 bond refinancing + EUR550m 2027 bond + RCF) -> 4.1% after 25% UK tax; gross debt GBP791m against c.GBP4.6bn market cap -> ~15% debt weight -> WACC c.8.7%, rounded to 8.5% given net debt ex-leases of only GBP23m. SAME WACC in all three scenarios: execution risk (fixed-price charges), UK MOD concentration and the governance history are charged ONCE, in the flows (base-case margin held 0.3-0.5pp below the >9% target as a recurring-charge allowance; bear weight lifted to 25%) - no ad-hoc WACC premium stacked on top.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Full FY26 lease cash of GBP61.6m (GBP44.5m principal, financing cash flow 'Lease payments'; GBP17.1m interest on lease liabilities, note 26) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.2% of revenue. Lease liabilities (GBP306.3m) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (GBP85.2m = PPE GBP67.5m + software amortisation; ROU depreciation GBP50.4m and acquired-intangible amortisation excluded). EBITDA margin anchor is therefore the IFRS-16 EBITDA (pre-lease) with SBC added back: FY26 ex-Type 31 = 433.3 UOP + 85.2 D&A + 50.4 ROU dep + 17.2 SBC = GBP586.1m = 11.3% of revenue; the build's FY0 EBIT of 586.1 - 61.6 - 17.2 - 85.2 = GBP422.1m ties to UOP ex-charge 433.3 less lease interest 17.1 plus (ROU dep 50.4 - principal 44.5).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial (GBP0.5m of FY26 profit, GBP2.0m dividends) and is ignored; flows are treated as 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: non-US operating industrial, with the adaptations for leases, pence quote and non-operating assets). Babcock is a defence/nuclear engineering-services contractor with real unlevered cash flows; not a bank, REIT or holdco. FIRST valuation of this ticker - no prior Drivers/DCF, no memory entry. ANCHORS: FY26 (year to 31 Mar 2026) revenue GBP5,177.7m (+8% organic); underlying operating profit GBP293.3m after a GBP140m Type 31 frigate charge, GBP433.3m / 8.2% margin excluding it; underlying EBITDA (covenant) GBP380.0m. The Type 31 charge was ENTIRELY NON-CASH in FY26 (contract liabilities +GBP95.5m from the revenue reversal, provisions +c.GBP45m), which is why reported cash conversion printed 119% vs 84% ex-charge; its cash cost falls in FY27-FY29 as the five ships are completed, so it is deducted once in the equity bridge (PV -GBP125m) rather than smeared through the margin path. last_fcf = reported FCF 242.1 (OCF 402.4 - capex 160.3) - SBC 17.2 - finance income 35.0 = 189.9; note that figure is still levered (GBP55.2m interest paid inside OCF) and flattered by the non-cash charge - the forward build is unlevered, ex-charge and component-built, so last_fcf is an anchor for the record, not the projection base. Interest/finance income (GBP35.0m) is stripped because the GBP723.6m cash and GBP44.9m finance-lease receivables sit in the bridge. Working capital: ex-Type 31 the FY26 movement was c.-GBP110m and FY25 -GBP39m (advance-payment unwind on existing contracts, Africa inventory) despite GBP786m of contract liabilities, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE in all scenarios (-15% base: growth consumes cash). Capex: FY26 gross GBP160.3m includes c.GBP51m of aircraft bought and sold-and-leased-back within the year (net capex GBP107.2m); base uses 2.6% of revenue trending to 2.3% with D&A ex-ROU rising from 1.65% to 2.0% as the Rosyth/advanced-manufacturing programme depreciates. Cash tax GBP18.3m (FY25 GBP21.8m) against ex-charge PBT of c.GBP424m: a GBP73.3m net deferred tax asset (UK losses, pensions) is sheltering cash tax; ramped 12% -> 25% UK statutory over five years. Pension: IAS 19 net deficit GBP34.0m but technical-provisions deficit c.GBP100m and guided deficit-repair of c.GBP20m p.a. (FY26 GBP18.5m) - deducted in the bridge, not perpetuated in the margin. DATA HYGIENE: Extracted/BAB.L_Annual_FY2025.txt and BAB.L_Presentation_2026.txt are Babcock & Wilcox (NYSE: BW) filings, not Babcock International; the CSV FY2025 row ties to the FY2026 annual report's comparatives and is correct, but those two files should be replaced. Buyback: GBP155.3m of own shares purchased in FY26 (financing cash flow) - the flat count IS being funded. House/street band is narrow (SBC 0.33% of revenue) but non-zero, so band_position is reported.

bear.growth_rationale: UK Defence Investment Plan slips under fiscal strain, FMSP follow-on re-priced on the bridging agreement, Rail and South Africa keep shrinking, exports stay LoIs; growth settles at 2-3% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: EBIT stalls at c.7.3% (EBITDA 10.8%): further Type 31 / Virginia-class / SMR fixed-price charges recur at c.GBP50-70m a year, the >9% target is never reached, and advance-payment unwind keeps working capital at -25% of growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 6% vs FY26 +8% organic and c.70% of FY27 revenue contracted at 1 April; decelerating through management's mid-single-digit medium-term average to 2.5% as the backlog (GBP9.8bn, 1.9x revenue, down from GBP10.4bn) is worked through.
base.margin_rationale: IFRS-16 EBITDA with SBC added back from 11.3% (FY26 ex-charge) to 12.2%, i.e. EBIT (after lease cash, SBC, D&A ex-ROU) from 8.15% to c.8.7% - the >9% target less a 0.3-0.5pp allowance for the recurring fixed-price contract charges (Type 31 FY26, SDP, Ascent) that Babcock's record says will keep arriving.

bull.growth_rationale: UK defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2027 and 3% ambition, AUKUS Rosyth work for HII, Indonesia MPP / Arrowhead 140 licences and Poland convert, Cavendish SMR owner's engineer scales; high-single-digit growth sustained four years.
bull.margin_rationale: EBIT reaches c.9.8% (EBITDA 13.3%) as Nuclear (already 9.5%) becomes a larger share, Aviation scales and no further large fixed-price charges land; export licence fees and deposits cut the working-capital drag to -5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: one customer (UK MOD c.61% of revenue, FMSP on a bridging agreement), a documented record of fixed-price charges and 2019-20 restatements, and a CEO transition in CY2026. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs three independent things - UK budget delivery, export conversion (Indonesia/Poland) and clean Type 31 completion - to all go right. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: sanity_check.py historical_table() multiplied the GBp price series by fx_rate=100 instead of dividing (GBP reporting / GBp LSE quote, same-currency pence/pound case like ABF.L/ADM.L/AAF.L) -- see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict. Printed P/B up to 94,104x and EV/EBITDA up to 136,609x are the script bug, not the company. See sanity_check_note for the hand-bridged true multiples.

sanity_check_note.issue: scripts/sanity_check.py historical_table() applies fx_rate=100 by multiplication where division is needed to convert the GBp (pence) price series to GBP (pounds) to match the GBP-denominated financials. Known defect, same shape as ABF.L, ADM.L, ABDN.L, AAF.L -- see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict.md.
sanity_check_note.method: Hand-bridged: FY-end price (nearest monthly close <= 31 March) divided by 100 to get GBP, then standard P/E (SBC-adjusted), P/B, EV/EBITDA (SBC-adjusted), P/Sales.
sanity_check_note.verdict: Genuine pass. Implied multiples at the base-case IV (P/E 27.3x, P/B 8.42x, EV/EBITDA 12.3x) sit at or slightly above FY2026 actuals (the top of the 7-year range) but do not exceed them by a wide margin -- consistent with a stock re-rating on improving UK/NATO defence spending sentiment that the market has already started to price in at the current £9.22 quote. No fix applied; passed is forced to false below only because the automated check ran on the corrupted (x100-too-high) comparison, not because the hand-bridged multiples look wrong.
